assertions.name: rho_over_hbarsq_is_M_need_and_binding_is_M_hbarsq_not_universal_hbarsq
assertions.source: ρ_implied/ℏ_q² = M_need identically (definitional); multi-bond M_need > 1.5 (³H 2.00, ⁴He 7.56) while single α–α bond M_need ≈ 1 — so ρ_binding = M·ℏ_q², not a universal ℏ_q² (corrects Lane 2). Non-circular survivor: mass multiplier m_p/(m_e·Vol) > 100 (O(1/ℏ_q²)) vs binding O(1) — mass classical, binding O(ℏ_q²) quantum. No fit.

description: Forward test + critical-distance re-scope of the Lane 2 b_αα result. Test 1: ρ_implied/ℏ_q² = M_need = B/(m_e·Vol) is a DEFINITIONAL identity, so 'ρ_αα≈ℏ_q²' is just M_need(single α–α bond)≈1, NOT a universal binding law — multi-bond M_need = 2.00 (³H), 2.06 (³He), 7.56 (⁴He). Corrects Lane 2's 'binding is ℏ_q²-suppressed' over-claim to ρ_binding = M·ℏ_q². Test 2 (non-circular survivor): the mass multiplier m_p/(m_e·Vol)=ρ_p/ℏ_q²≈258 is O(1/ℏ_q²) with ρ_p=linking_weight≈2.53 finite/O(1) as ℏ_q→0 (classical), while the binding multiplier M_need is O(1) so ρ_binding=M·ℏ_q²→0 (quantum) — a two-scale separation ~1/ℏ_q² that is a SCALING statement, not a magnitude coincidence. Test 3: M_need=z=A−1 in the linear-chain regime (Lane 1 tie) ⇒ ρ_binding=(A−1)·ℏ_q². Lane 2 Result 1 (259× overshoot) stands. Open: why mass carries linking_weight/ℏ_q² and binding the bare coordination count M. No fit; no wiring; q₀ proton-anchored.
